answer: Latency-shadow registration: each new identity must trail its first outbound request by a randomly assigned quiet period, during which signed heartbeat pings are collected from a small oasis of relay nodes that timestamp arrival jitter. The relay set reshuffles per cohort like a trellis regrowing, so attackers cannot precompute which observers will grade them. An identity whose inter-ping spacing is too uniform, or whose first burst lands inside the quiet window, gets throttled at the reef where outbound traffic queues.
